Moderator logistics, promotions and audience assertions are not participant achievements; a speaker’s adoption or answer is eligible. No prior debate’s editor scope applies.

The moderator introduces speakers and reads attributed audience prompts. He has no sustained independent advocacy. Treat quoted super-chat taunts as prompts, never as an additional speaker’s scored argument or as claims endorsed by either opponent. Preserve question context when it makes an answer intelligible. If an apparent host argument or uncertain speaker ownership is found, flag it before acceptance rather than quietly dropping substantive material.

The last caption is closing music, so the slight end overshoot reflects caption duration, not missing content. No direct audio listening is claimed. Events overlap in time but are sequential caption text, not duplicated rolling transcripts; preserve canonical words and timestamps.

This restriction does not shield the speaker’s clearly expressed assumptions or inferential claims from ordinary assessment.

Cross-examination and Q&A have mixed speakers; a passage cannot receive high attribution merely because its topic favors one side.
